records.title: Toward True Neutrality: Evaluating Inference-Time Debiasing Strategies for Gender Coreference Resolution in LLMs
records.venue: Proceedings of the 39th Pacific Asia Conference on Language, Information and Computation
records.version_status: official PACLIC 2025 proceedings version; no preprint found
records.peer_review_evidence: ACL Anthology records the paper in the PACLIC 2025 proceedings.
records.eligibility_technical: Compares self-correction, self-consistency and chain-of-thought for occupational gender coreference while measuring bias reduction and computational cost; low-bias-feedback self-correction improves performance by up to 41 percent over self-consistent prompting.
records.eligibility_social: Directly addresses gender bias affecting women and non-binary people in a task motivated by healthcare, education and finance deployments.
notes: The study also qualitatively analyzes bias, logic and grammaticality patterns in chain-of-thought responses.
No DOI is listed in ACL Anthology.

records.title: Prompting Fairness: Integrating Causality to Debias Large Language Models
records.version_status: arXiv v1 2024-03-13, v2 2025-03-02; official ICLR 2025 conference paper
records.peer_review_evidence: Official ICLR 2025 proceedings record and OpenReview conference-paper record.
records.eligibility_technical: Develops a causality-guided debiasing framework and Dual Directional Prompting; evaluates black-box LLMs on WinoBias and BBQ. On WinoBias, GPT-4 reaches a 2.17 percent pro/anti gap and 94.57 percent accuracy on anti-stereotypical cases.
records.eligibility_social: Targets gender and broader social bias and explicitly motivates the method with high-stakes hiring and healthcare decisions.
notes: This is distinct from the locally present work Prompting fairness: Learning prompts for debiasing large language models.
Open preprint landing page: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08743

records.title: Gender Bias in LLM Hiring Decisions: Evidence from a Japanese Context and Evaluation of Mitigation Strategies
records.version_status: arXiv v1; no accepted conference or journal version found by the cutoff date
records.peer_review_evidence: No peer-review evidence found; preprint only.
records.eligibility_technical: Counterfactual design with 60 Japanese rirekisho resumes, 12 gender-signaling name pairs, five LLMs and 43200 API calls across baseline, gender-neutrality instruction and privacy-filter conditions. The prompt instruction does not meaningfully reduce bias; removing names removes nearly the full effect.
records.eligibility_social: Direct gender-bias evidence in hiring, with a non-Western setting and practical privacy/refusal trade-offs relevant to personnel and case decisions.
notes: The privacy-filter condition produces a 42 percent refusal rate for GPT-4o.
Findings remain provisional because the work is not peer reviewed.

records.title: Mitigating medical bias in large language models by prompt engineering: an empirical study of effectiveness and trade-offs
records.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A, 384(2324), article 20250125
records.version_status: version of record; no preprint found
records.peer_review_evidence: Published as a journal article by the Royal Society in Philosophical Transactions A.
records.eligibility_technical: Evaluates five prompting strategies across five LLMs on a medical-bias benchmark, jointly measuring fairness, accuracy and inference overhead. Chain-of-thought reduces the average group gap by 2.4 percentage points, with a maximum reduction of 6.2 points and significant reductions in 8 of 15 McNemar comparisons.
records.eligibility_social: Directly addresses fair healthcare and patient-safety risks for groups defined by sensitive attributes.
notes: No prompting strategy is universally effective, and some exacerbate bias.
The VOR is registered under CC BY 4.0, but automated publisher retrieval returned HTTP 403 in this environment.
Authoritative abstract and metadata: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42463224/

records.title: Rethinking Prompt-based Debiasing in Large Language Model
records.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025
records.version_status: arXiv preprint submitted 2025-03-12 under the plural title Large Language Models; Findings of ACL version published 2025-07 under the singular title Large Language Model
records.peer_review_evidence: ACL Anthology records the paper in Findings of ACL 2025.
records.eligibility_technical: Evaluates prompt-based debiasing on BBQ and StereoSet with open models and GPT; shows that lower bias scores can result from evasive Unknown responses and reduced task accuracy. Llama2-7B-Chat misclassified more than 90 percent of unbiased content as biased.
records.eligibility_social: Provides a necessary validity check for claimed social-bias mitigation and for evaluations used to justify deployment in socially sensitive contexts.
notes: The paper argues that fairness, task accuracy and answer evasion must be evaluated together.
Open preprint landing page: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09219

records.title: Multi-Persona Thinking for Bias Mitigation in Large Language Models
records.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026
records.version_status: arXiv v1 2026-01-21, v3 2026-04-21; Findings of ACL version published 2026-07
records.peer_review_evidence: ACL Anthology records the paper in Findings of ACL 2026.
records.eligibility_technical: Introduces an inference-time multi-persona framework in which contrasting social identities and a neutral perspective iteratively identify and correct biased judgments; evaluated on two established bias benchmarks with open and closed models.
records.eligibility_social: Explicitly models male, female and neutral viewpoints and addresses harmful social stereotypes and unfair outcomes.
notes: The authors report lower bias than existing prompting-based methods while maintaining core reasoning ability.
Open preprint landing page: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.15488

records.title: Patient Cognitive Bias in Large Language Model-Supported Health Consultations: Simulation-Based Comparative Study
records.venue: Journal of Medical Internet Research, 28, e85770
records.version_status: JMIR preprint submitted 2025-10-13, accepted 2026-05-04; journal version published 2026-06-11
records.peer_review_evidence: JMIR records the original paper and an explicit submitted/accepted open-review history.
records.eligibility_technical: Uses 1273 MedQA-USMLE cases, six LLMs, three-round consultations, three prompt mitigations and four temperature settings. Patient bias reduces accuracy by about 7-39 percentage points; prompting is limited and inconsistent, while a separate reasoning system gains about 10-39 points.
records.eligibility_social: Directly evaluates patient-facing health consultations and user-driven cognitive bias in an interactive Human Services setting.
notes: The all-inclusive prompt provides the most consistent but generally modest prompt-level gains.
Open review/version landing page: https://preprints.jmir.org/preprint/85770/accepted

records.title: Prompting Techniques for Reducing Social Bias in LLMs through System 1 and System 2 Cognitive Processes
records.venue: Proceedings of the 15th International Conference on Recent Advances in Natural Language Processing (RANLP 2025)
records.version_status: arXiv v1 2024-04-26, v4 2025-08-22; accepted main-conference proceedings version published 2025-09
records.peer_review_evidence: The arXiv record states Accepted at RANLP-2025 (main conference); ACL Anthology records the proceedings paper.
records.eligibility_technical: Compares zero-shot CoT, direct debiasing, System 1/System 2 prompts and human/machine personas across five LLMs, two datasets and nine social-bias categories; reports up to a 33 percent reduction in stereotypical judgments.
records.eligibility_social: Directly covers gender, race, religion, nationality, profession and other social categories and is closely aligned with socially sensitive prompt design.
notes: The local registry contains the arXiv preprint but not the RANLP 2025 proceedings version.
The most effective prompt combination varies by model and bias category.
Open preprint landing page: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.17218
